newsitem.title: USA: Clinton calls for democracy in Cuba.
newsitem.headline: Clinton calls for democracy in Cuba.

text.p: One year after Cuba shot down two U.S. civilian planes, U.S. President Bill Clinton honoured the incident's four victims on Monday and called for a peaceful transition to democracy in Cuba.

"The shoot-down and the Cuban government's continuing repression of human rights activists and independent journalists underscore the need to continue working for a peaceful transition to democracy in Cuba," Clinton said in a statement.

Described the attack that chilled already frosty relations between Washington and Havana, he said: "One year ago, four innocent civilians were killed when their aircraft were brutally shot down by the Cuban regime. Without warning, Cuban MiGs fired air-to-air missiles at two small unarmed planes in international air space."
Clinton said he joined the victims' families "in honouring the memory of these men as we carry forward our efforts to seek justice for their deaths."

Four Cuban-Americans were killed in the attack. They belonged to Brothers to the Rescue, a group opposed to Cuban leader Fidel Castro that flew missions over the Florida Straits to find rafters leaving Communist-ruled Cuba.

The downings brought outrage against Cuba, but also hurt relations between Washington and its allies by prompting the Helms-Burton Act, which tightened the U.S. economic embargo on Cuba by seeking to punish investors from other countries.
